items.front: 1991 crisis — trigger, forex level, who led reforms?
items.back: BoP crisis: forex ~US$1.2 bn (2–3 weeks' imports); Gulf War oil spike. India pledged gold + took IMF bailout. LPG reforms by PM P.V. Narasimha Rao & FM Manmohan Singh.
items.examPoint: The 1991 crisis and the LPG reforms
items.source: notes

items.front: Post-1991 outcomes — which rose, which fell?
items.back: Rose: export share in world trade, FDI, forex reserves. Fell: agriculture's share in GDP. (Classic UPSC 2017 statement item.)
items.examPoint: The 1991 crisis and the LPG reforms
items.source: notes

items.front: BoP — sort: FDI, remittances, portfolio, SDRs.
items.back: Current account: remittances/transfers, trade, invisibles, SDRs. Capital/financial account: FDI, portfolio (FII), loans/ECB. Overall BoP always balances (double-entry).
items.examPoint: Balance of Payments — Structure & Convertibility
items.source: notes

items.front: FDI vs FPI/FII; what is a P-Note?
items.back: FDI = long-term, control, DPIIT/RBI, stable. FPI/FII = portfolio, no control, volatile 'hot money', SEBI. Participatory Note lets overseas investors access Indian market without SEBI registration.
items.examPoint: FDI vs FPI vs FII, Routes & Sectoral Caps
items.source: notes

items.front: Rupee convertibility — current vs capital account.
items.back: Current-account convertible since Aug 1994 (IMF Article VIII); capital-account convertibility only partial (Tarapore Committees 1997, 2006). Convertibility = free two-way conversion.
items.examPoint: Balance of Payments — Structure & Convertibility
items.source: notes

items.front: WTO — year, HQ, two core principles.
items.back: Established 1 Jan 1995 (Marrakesh Agreement 1994), succeeding GATT; HQ Geneva. MFN = no discrimination between partners; National Treatment = foreign & domestic goods treated equally.
items.examPoint: WTO — Structure, Principles & Agreements
items.source: notes

items.front: Amber, blue, green boxes belong to which agreement?
items.back: WTO Agreement on Agriculture subsidies: Amber = trade-distorting (capped/AMS); Blue = production-limiting (allowed); Green = non/minimally distorting (allowed). NOT environment — classic trap.
items.examPoint: WTO — Structure, Principles & Agreements
items.source: notes

items.front: Peace Clause, TFA, TRIMS — quick facts.
items.back: Peace Clause = Bali 2013, protects food-security (MSP) procurement. TFA = Bali 2013, in force Feb 2017. TRIMS = trade-related investment measures, goods only. SPS = food-safety/health standards.
items.examPoint: WTO — Structure, Principles & Agreements
items.source: notes

items.front: Who publishes: Global Competitiveness Report, Ease of Doing Business?
items.back: Global Competitiveness Report = World Economic Forum (WEF). Ease of Doing Business = World Bank (discontinued 2021). BTIA = India–EU FTA.
items.examPoint: WTO — Structure, Principles & Agreements
items.source: notes

items.front: IMF SDR basket & AIIB largest shareholder?
items.back: SDR basket: USD, EUR, RMB/Renminbi (added 2016), GBP, JPY. AIIB (2016, HQ Beijing) — China is the largest shareholder, India 2nd; has non-Asian members. NDB (BRICS) HQ Shanghai.
items.examPoint: FDI vs FPI vs FII, Routes & Sectoral Caps
items.source: notes

items.front: Recent FTAs — CEPA, ECTA, TEPA, CETA partners.
items.back: CEPA=UAE (2022), ECTA=Australia (2022), TEPA=EFTA (in force Oct 2025, US$100bn pledge), CETA=UK (signed 24 Jul 2025, in force 15 Jul 2026). India withdrew from RCEP in 2019.
items.examPoint: Foreign Trade Policy 2023 & Recent FTAs
items.source: notes

items.front: FTP 2023 — nature and headline target.
items.back: Effective 1 Apr 2023 under DGFT; dynamic/open-ended (no sunset). Target: US$2 trillion exports (goods+services) by 2030. India is the largest rice exporter.
items.examPoint: Foreign Trade Policy 2023 & Recent FTAs
items.source: notes

items.front: Name three trade reforms after 1991.
items.back: Tariff cuts, removal of quantitative restrictions on imports, and Special Economic Zones (SEZs) for exports.
